claims.text: The studied alloy has the composition Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Very rapid quenching can produce an initially amorphous Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy.
The amorphous alloy is prone to a multistep crystallization sequence during conventional reheating.
The proposed intervention is an ultrafast UF-DSC pulse reheating step at a heating rate greater than 10^4 K/min immediately after rapid cooling.
Cooling at approximately 10^3 K/s is sufficient to retain an amorphous state in this alloy.
During rapid cooling, a thermal transformation designated T3 occurs at approximately 977 K.
A reheating temperature below or near 977 K lies below the onset or nucleation threshold for primary crystallization.
Ultrafast pulse reheating will suppress nucleation and growth of primary crystalline phases.
A brief ultrafast heating pulse minimizes residence time at temperatures favorable for nucleation.
Reducing residence time limits diffusion-driven phase separation and crystalline ordering.
Ultrafast pulse reheating will delay or suppress exothermic crystallization peaks relative to conventional reheating.
Ultrafast pulse reheating will retain a higher amorphous fraction than conventional reheating.
Ultrafast pulse reheating will enhance the alloy's thermal stability.
Under conventional DSC reheating, the alloy exhibits multistep crystallization with extensive primary-phase formation.
The intervention should be effective only when applied immediately after rapid cooling and at temperatures approximately below 977 K.
The efficacy of the intervention will diminish with slower reheating or reheating substantially above 977 K.
The critical heating rate and effective temperature window may vary with microstructural heterogeneity.
Similar crystallization exotherms and crystalline phase fractions in ultrafast-pulse and conventional-reheating samples would falsify the proposed improvement.
